paper_title: Endgames in Fog of War Chess
classifications: Theory of computation → Solution concepts in game theory
source_locator: Explicit open question on PDF page 19
statement: Proof. Without loss of generality, let the White king be on A1, and the two rooks on A2 (Rook 1) and B1 (Rook 2). The following strategy resembles the staircase mate in classical chess, but we have to be more careful, as we do not know the exact position of the Black king. Therefore, we have to cover the rooks with the White king such that the Black king cannot take one of them. The strategy proceeds as follows and can be repeated until checkmate: Move Rook 2 up one square. Move Rook 1 up one square. Move the White king one square up. As in classical chess, this forces the Black king to move up (and right), as otherwise White would capture him. Eventually, the Black king has no moves left to escape. ◀
context: Then there is a strategy such that White always wins. Proof. Without loss of generality, let the White king be on A1, and the two rooks on A2 (Rook 1) and B1 (Rook 2). The following strategy resembles the staircase mate in classical chess, but we have to be more careful, as we do not know the exact position of the Black king. Therefore, we have to cover the rooks with the White king such that the Black king cannot take one of them. The strategy proceeds as follows and can be repeated until checkmate: Move Rook 2 up one square. Move Rook 1 up one square. Move the White king one square up. As in classical chess, this forces the Black king to move up (and right), as otherwise White would capture him. Eventually, the Black king has no moves left to escape. ◀ ▶ Corollary 22. Given that White starts with a king and two rooks, and Black with a king. White begins and knows the initial position of the Black king. Then White wins. 5 Final Comments and Open Questions We showed that in Fog of War chess, given that one player has a king and queen and plays against a lone king, he can always guarantee a win. In contrast to classical chess, if one player has a king and a rook, then he cannot guarantee a win against a player with a lone king. However, adding one more rook for the player with the rook guarantees a win for him.
